question.text: Consider a TCP connection where the congestion window size is 60 KB when a packet loss is detected via a timeout. The connection has a round trip time of 80 msec and uses a maximum segment size of 4 KB . The time taken (in msec) by the TCP connection to increase its congestion window back to 60 KB is $\_\_\_\_$ .

question.text: A communication channel over a transatlantic fiber-optic link is managed using a selective repeat sliding window protocol. The protocol uses a frame size of 2 KB to send data over the 10 Mbps link, which has a one-way propagation delay of 40 msec . To achieve a minimum link utilization of $80 \%$, the minimum number of bits required for the sequence number field is $\_\_\_\_$ .
question.subject: Computer Networks

question.text: A network architect is designing a network segment based on the Fast Ethernet standard, which operates at a transmission speed of 100 Mbps . The design specifies a maximum segment length of 200 meters between any two stations. If the signal propagation speed in the cable is $2 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$, what is the minimum frame size (in bits) that must be enforced on this network to ensure that the CSMA/CD protocol can reliably detect collisions?
question.subject: Computer Networks

question.text:
A server ( S ) sends a 4 Megabit ( $4 \times 10^{6}$ bits) file to a client (D). The path between S and D consists of three routers, creating a total of four links. The file is segmented into 2000 packets of equal size. Each of the four links has a length of 200 km and a bandwidth of 10 Mbps . If the signal propagation speed over the links is $2 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, what is the total end-to-end delay to send the entire file? (Assume there is no queuing or processing delay).

A. 400 ms

B. 404 ms

C. 1600 ms

D. 1604 ms
question.subject: Computer Networks

question.text: A ground station transmits a data packet of 2000 bytes to a satellite orbiting at an altitude of 4500 km . The communication link has a bandwidth of 200 Mbps , and the signal travels at the speed of light, approximately $3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Calculate the total time (in milliseconds, rounded off to two decimal places) for the entire packet to be received by the satellite.
